summary: A 1934 CCC-built 59-ft-3-in International Derrick tower in Chenango County; active until 1988, closed 1989, restored and reopened to the public in September 2021.

facts.design: 59-foot-3-inch International Derrick tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

access.note: Open for recreation since September 13, 2021, after a DEC restoration. DEC calls it the only fire tower open for recreation on public lands in Central New York.

visit.hours: open to the public year-round, sunrise to sunset (DEC, 2021)

notes_for_editor: Three independent sources agree on the 1934 CCC build, the 1988 end of fire watch, the early-1989 closure and the September 13, 2021 reopening. The NHLR page gives no build year, so 1934 comes from the DEC release and Wikipedia. The 1935 first-staffing date rests on Wikipedia alone. The DEC release says the tower was open for recreation after the upgrades; access is recorded as public, climbable true, on that basis. Current staffing is not documented after the 2017 NHLR visit (not staffed). An andyarthur.org page gives an early-fall 1934 construction date, but it could not be fetched, so it is not used. The DEC release's sentence on a Forest Service chapter agreement was cut off in the cache and is not used. Height is 59 ft 3 in per Wikipedia (18.06 m). The NHLR visit report predates the 2021 work, so its condition findings are historical. Verification pass 2026-10-08: the story's visitor-rules sentence had no support in the DEC release and was replaced with the DEC's sunrise-to-sunset hours; the 1,960 ft figure is from the NHLR and DEC, and Wikipedia's 1,962 ft is named in the story; 'no one had a key' was corrected to the report's 'we had no key'.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and DEC give 1,960 ft (597 m); Wikipedia gives 1,962 ft (598 m). The story reports 1,960 ft and names Wikipedia's figure.
